answer.location_description: Bottom-left corner of the image, roughly rows 18-22 and columns 0-3, a small patch along the left edge near the bottom, well away from the centred nodule.
answer.mechanism: Two groups of first-layer units read this corner with opposite signs. The positive-bias 'benign' units (3, 5, 14, 15, 19, 21, 23, 24, 26, 28) have strong negative weights there, so a bright corner shuts them off. Unit 3 alone contributes about -18k (integer product units) to the logit through layer 2 (u2, u8, u9, u15 and others), so turning these units off removes benign evidence. The negative-bias 'malignant' units (11, 16, 27, 30, plus 0 and 20) have strong positive weights in the same patch. Unit 27 contributes about +20k to the logit through u1, u2, u8, u11 and u15, so a bright patch switches these units on and pushes the logit positive. Both pathways move the output toward malignant.
answer.evidence: Benign-side units, rows 19-21 x cols 0-2: unit 3 sums to -361 (r20: -54 -64 -32), unit 15 to -346 (r20: -49 -52 -50), unit 5 to -306 (r20: -45 -56 -55), unit 28 to -260 (r19: -47 -40 -54). Units 19, 21, 23, 24 and 26 also sit at about -30 to -57 there. Malignant-side units in the same place: unit 11 r19 = 43 63 67 30; unit 27 r19-r21 = 8 39 52 46 / 48 26 57 24 / 21 9 39 49; unit 16 r18-r19 = 48 -8 42 / 47 34 15 34; unit 30 r21-r22 = 39 22 51 / 22 34 41 34. Weights elsewhere at the periphery are mostly small and mixed, about ±30. There is a weaker, more diffuse version at the top-right (row 0, cols 16-23), but at matched 3x3 patches it is about half as strong, so the compact bottom-left patch is the most consistent off-nodule feature. It is far outside the 12-pixel nodule region and has no anatomical reason to be in the same place in every rescaled crop.
answer.main_feature: Centre-focused templates over the nodule (roughly rows 5-17, cols 5-19). The weights encode nodule size, shape and margin, contrasting a compact, sharply bounded bright nodule ring (benign-leaning units) with irregular or extended bright structure and dark-ring patterns around the nodule (malignant-leaning units).
